security_implications: The chunk declares secret_key (1024-bit), key_length, wipe_secret, and digest-size controls, all of which are central to HMAC security. The width of secret_key combined with key_length handling risks exposing unused key bits if the masking logic is not enforced. The wipe_secret signal implies a zeroization requirement; failure to wipe completely could leave key material reachable. Digest size configuration directly determines hash strength; an illegal digest mode could yield a weak output. Alert and error paths are also declared, affecting integrity reporting. These signals require rigorous cross-block analysis to ensure no key leakage, proper zeroization, and correct digest sizing.
